messages:
emily: thinking out loud — we need a synthetic generator that can 1) produce a sawtooth/QPS ramp, 2) inject short high-frequency bursts, and 3) vary KV cache warm fraction so we can correlate cache hit-rate with p50/p99 shifts. anyone prototyped this pattern?

raj: I built a basic sawtooth in the old harness. It ramps qps linearly up/down over a period and adds jitter. but we never exposed a per-request kv_warm boolean to control cache state. good idea to make that explicit.

marco: major concern: kernel selection changes with sequence length + batch shape. if our generator mixes tiny bursts with long sequences we may trigger different kernel branches and confound the comparison. need "apples-to-apples" controls: pin seq len distribution, force kernel hints if possible.

sara: +1. also turn off autoscaling and burst smoothing in the infra so the runtime isn't hiding microbursts. run on dedicated harness with fixed capacity.

emily: proposed generator config (proto):

```
# sawtooth_sampler config
period_sec: 120          # full up+down cycle
min_qps: 5
max_qps: 250
burst_spike_qps: 1200    # short microbursts layered on top
burst_duration_ms: 150
burst_probability_per_sec: 0.03
kv_warm_fraction_schedule: [0.1, 0.5, 0.9]  # rotate by epoch
seq_len_distribution: fixed(256)           # keep seq len pinned for kernel parity
batch_target_tokens: 1024
random_seed: 314159
```

raj: if we rotate kv_warm_fraction between epochs, we can compute per-epoch hit-rate and join that with latency histograms. make sure request ids are logged so we can correlate with KV cache state.

marco: for kernel parity tests add these controls: force `kernel_hint=fused` and `kernel_hint=split_attn` runs, and run both on same hardware image. small diff in environment will blow up p99.

sara: runbook checklist for apples-to-apples:
- pin model repo commit and quantization bitwidth
- disable runtime auto-fallback (so we detect perf regressions)
- prefill KV cache to given warm_fraction per epoch
- disable external caches/CDN
- run each test 5x and capture med/iqr/p99

perf-bot: CI run summary (from latest PR harness)
```
run: sawtooth-kv-correlation-1718999999
hardware: g5.16xlarge (one node)
kernel=fused, kv_warm=0.1 -> p50=42ms p95=210ms p99=380ms
kernel=split_attn, kv_warm=0.1 -> p50=40ms p95=200ms p99=360ms
kernel=fused, kv_warm=0.9 -> p50=32ms p95=120ms p99=260ms
kernel=split_attn, kv_warm=0.9 -> p50=31ms p95=115ms p99=255ms
note: observed ~6% p99 regression for fused vs split_attn at low warm fraction
```

emily: hmm that matches the hypothesis: fused kernel does worse on cold-KV workload at tail. could be batching heuristics underutilizing token batching when KV misses cause longer per-request time.

raj: action items:
- extend harness to support per-request kv_warm toggle and logging (raj)
- add kernel_hint switch in generator harness so we can sweep (marco)
- create a dashboard combining kv_hit_rate vs pxx (sara)
- add a short script to reproduce the perf-bot run with deterministic seed (emily)

marco: idea: instrument the runtime to emit a small marker when a request hits a different kernel branch (so we can split latency histograms by kernel decision). cheap metric: kernel_choice counter tagged by seq_len, batch_size, kv_hit.

sara: also record batching histograms (batch sizes over time) — microbursts can collapse batching which explains tail spikes. add `batch_size` field to request logs.

emily: quick repro command I used locally:
```
./harness/run_sawtooth --config sawtooth_sampler.yaml --kernel-hint fused --fixed-capacity 1 --log-requests --seed 314159
```

raj: remember to run with `--prefill-kv` mode to reach target warm fractions before the measurement epoch. otherwise the first minute will bias results.

marco: we'll want one long run (30m) per config and a short stress run (3m with lots of microbursts) to validate long-tail behavior.

emily: OK I'll prototype the kv_warm toggle and add a small CSV output that has per-request: ts, req_id, seq_len, batch_at_serve, kernel_choice, kv_hit, latency_ms. that will let us do post-join analyses.

sara: thanks — feel free to drop any interim runs in #eng-runtime. happy to eyeball histograms and sanity-check infra settings. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: linked artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/sawtooth/1718999999/ (logs + flamegraphs)
